subject: Post-demo follow-up: context-window assessment + model recommendations
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medrec.health>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: context-window assessment + model recommendations

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the product demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so we can scope a short pilot that validates long-context behavior for your visit notes ingestion use case. I kept this tight and action-oriented.

Recap (what we heard)
- Volume: ~5M notes/year, typical single-patient history spans 25–80 pages; median sequence length during retrieval ~20k tokens.
- Primary failures you care about: truncation of prior visit history causing missed context; hallucinated medication changes in summaries; latency target <=600ms for API reads in interactive clinician UI.
- Security: SOC2 + regional data residency are blockers for production.

Initial model recommendations (to evaluate in pilot)
1) redwood-compat-30b-q4f: good cost / latency balance for batch summarization of long visits; supports 32k context in our optimized runtime with prefix KV caching.
2) llama3-70b-std-8k-extended: strong extractive fidelity on long documents in our benchmarks but requires dedicated GPU pool for interactive targets.
3) redwood-xt-7b-extended: low-cost candidate for fast, low-latency retrieval-augmented responses (good as fallback).

Benchmarks & prompt sets (attached / linked)
- context-window-benchmarks.csv — synthetic truncation sweep across 4k/8k/16k/32k with rouge & factuality flags. (attached)
- prompt-set-sample.jsonl — 25 prompts designed to stress multi-visit chronological reasoning, medication consistency checks, and concise clinical-summaries. (attached)
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleBenchmarkFolder

Quality/regression concerns to watch for in the pilot
- Summarization fidelity: measured by medication-precision / event-order errors. We recommend setting a baseline threshold: medication-precision >= 98% on curated sets.
- Truncation behavior: ensure prefix KV caching preserves earliest relevant visit tokens for extraction tasks — we'll run targeted KV retention tests.
- Hallucination gating: add a conservative verifier step (lightweight QA model) to flag low-confidence statements for clinician review.

Proposed next steps & timeline
1) Scope pilot dataset (you provide de-identified export for 200 patient timelines) — Elena confirm by Tues 12/2.
2) Redwood runs 2-week eval across the three model candidates (we provide benchmarks and a short dashboard).
3) Joint review + go/no-go for a 6-week canary (performance + fidelity acceptance).

Can we lock the dataset by 2026-12-02 and kick off the eval the week of 12/8?

Attachments: medrec-demo-notes.pdf (call slides), prompt-set-sample.jsonl, context-window-benchmarks.csv

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.inference

----

From: Elena Morales <elena@medrec.health>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 12:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: context-window assessment + model recommendations

Thanks Stephanie — this is very helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can produce a de-identified export for ~250 patients but need guidance on the schema and a checklist for PHI redaction; can you share the exact fields you need?
- On the medication-precision target: 98% sounds fair but we care more about false positives on medication additions (we want to minimize telling a clinician a medication was stopped/added when it wasn't).
- Latency: the interactive UI path is most critical; for batch nightly summarization we can tolerate higher latency.

I'll confirm dataset availability tomorrow. Also attaching the internal evaluation rubric we use for summaries (MedRec rubric v3).

Best,
Elena
Director of Clinical Data Products
MedRec Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: context-window assessment + model recommendations

Hi Elena — great to meet you on the call. Following up with the redaction checklist and the minimal schema we need to ingest the 250-patient export. See the linked doc (Drive) and attached sample schema file.

Quick items from our ops side:
- Data checklist: de-id required for name/SSN/phones; keep medical codes (ICD/LOINC) and timestamps (offset to relative days) — those are important for event-order tests.
- Pilot design: we'll run three model variants on the same dataset and compute: medication-precision, event-order accuracy, hallucination-rate, average latency at p50/p95.
- Token budget: for 32k window runs expect ~2–3x cost vs 8k runs; we can show cost tradeoffs in the dashboard.

Aditya will follow up with brief instructions for secure upload (S3 pre-signed + KMS envelope). Proposed kickoff: 2026-12-08.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.inference
